problem_motivation.content: There is a need to improve the fitting flexibility of Material Fingerprinting.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: To increase the fitting flexibility of Material Fingerprinting, we propose an adaptive model database coupled with an iterative pattern recognition algorithm that refines the material model in each step.

problem_motivation.content: Data-driven characterization methods still require optimization that may be expensive and unreliable.
problem_motivation.evidence_span:
Despite their enhanced fitting accuracy and broad applicability, all aforementioned data-driven material characteriza-
tion methods share the requirement of solving an optimization problem. Depending on the experimental setup and the
underlying material modeling assumptions, this optimization problem can be computationally expensive, non-convex,
and subject to nonlinear parameter constraints, such that convergence to a global optimum is often not guaranteed.

problem_motivation.content: Remaining discrepancies in the skin fit need explanation
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, for certain loading modes and stress components, deviations remain.

problem_motivation.content: Future work is needed on more deformation modes, inelasticity, alternative features, and automated hyperparameter tuning
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Future work may extend the database to additional deformation modes, explore inelastic material behavior, incorporate alternative feature sets, and further investigate automated strategies for hyperparameter tuning and model selection.

problem_motivation.content: Exponential feature evaluations can overflow at large deformations, motivating approximation.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: We note that some of the considered modeling features require the evaluation of the exponential function, which can lead to overflow errors for large deformations.

prior_approach.content: The authors previously proposed Material Fingerprinting for rapid discovery of mechanical material models without continuous optimization.
prior_approach.evidence_span: We recently proposed a method called Material Fingerprinting for the rapid discovery of mechanical material models that avoids solving continuous optimization problems.

prior_approach.content: Material Fingerprinting precomputes a database of fingerprints and uses pattern recognition to identify a model for unseen measurements.
prior_approach.evidence_span:
Material Fingerprinting is a novel method for the rapid discovery of material models (Flaschel et al., 2026a). It oper-
ates by precomputing a database of material responses, a.k.a. fingerprints, and their corresponding material models in
an offline stage, which is subsequently leveraged in an online stage to identify the appropriate material model for an
unseen experimental measurement via a pattern-recognition algorithm.

prior_approach.content: Classical material characterization assumes a constitutive form and fits parameters by minimizing mismatch to experiments.
prior_approach.evidence_span:
The classical strategy for material characterization is to assume a mathematical
description of the material behavior that depends on a set of material parameters, which are then identified by min-
imizing the mismatch between model predictions and experimentally measured data (Gdoutos and Konsta-Gdoutos,
2024).

prior_approach.content: Full-field methods characterize materials by minimizing mismatch with boundary-value simulations or PDE residuals.
prior_approach.evidence_span:
More specifically, the measured displacement fields and reaction forces can be used for
material characterization by minimizing the mismatch between experimental data and data predicted by simulations
of the corresponding boundary value problem, or by minimizing the residuals of the governing partial differential
equations, see the overviews by Avril et al. (2008); Roux and Hild (2020); Römer et al. (2025).

prior_approach.content: Modern data-driven characterization methods impose fewer assumptions on model form, including neural networks.
prior_approach.evidence_span:
In contrast to a priori assuming a material model and calibrating its parameters, modern methods for material char-
acterization impose fewer assumptions on the mathematical form of the material model, which promises enhanced
fitting accuracy. For example, neural networks can be used to represent mechanical material behavior (Ghaboussi
et al., 1991).

prior_approach.content: Other prior concise/interpretable discovery methods include symbolic regression, EUCLID, and CANNs.
prior_approach.evidence_span:
Another line of research focuses on the discovery of concise and inter-
pretable mathematical expressions for material models. Popular methods include symbolic regression (Abdusalamov
et al., 2023), the EUCLID approach (Flaschel et al., 2021; Flaschel, 2023), and CANNs (Linka and Kuhl, 2023; Linka
et al., 2023; Holthusen et al., 2024, 2026; Martonová et al., 2024, 2025).

prior_approach.content: In the extreme prior approach, simulations are driven directly by a database of stress-strain pairs instead of an explicit material model.
prior_approach.evidence_span:
Finally, in the extreme case, the formulation of the material model is omitted altogether, and simulations are
directly informed by a database of stress-strain pairs, which serves as a surrogate for the material model (Kirchdoer-
fer and Ortiz, 2016; Ibañez et al., 2017).

mechanism_principle.content: Because anisotropic invariant derivatives at the undeformed state are not identity-like, pressure alone cannot enforce zero stress there; thus anisotropic feature derivatives must vanish at F=I.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
For anisotropic features, in contrast, the derivatives ∂I/∂F do not reduce to the identity tensor. Hence, the
isotropic pressure term alone cannot enforce P = 0 in the undeformed configuration. To address this issue, we require
the first derivatives of the anisotropic feature functions to vanish at F = I. This additional condition motivates the
different design of the anisotropic features h compared to the isotropic features g.

mechanism_principle.content: Polyconvexity is guaranteed when g and h are convex and monotone, leading to simple parameter constraints.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
In particular, polyconvexity is ensured if the
functions g and h in Eq. (7)-Eq. (8) are convex and monotone, which leads to simple parameter constraints: gA requires
α ≥1, gB requires α ≥0, and gC requires α1 ≥0, while hB is admissible for α ≥0 and hA is excluded.

mechanism_principle.content: Because anisotropic stress depends on λa=F22 here, it affects only the P22 stress component under the standardized modes
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This expression shows that anisotropic contributions act exclusively on the P22 component of the first Piola-Kirchhoff stress tensor. Consequently, the additional terms introduced in the second adaptive step in Eq. (16), as well as the second and fourth terms in Eq. (17), affect only this stress component.

mechanism_principle.content: Separating offline database generation from online identification avoids continuous potentially nonconvex optimization
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: the separation into an offline database generation stage and an online identification stage avoids the solution of continuous, potentially non-convex optimization problems.

mechanism_principle.content: Because online discovery is algebraic operations and similarity searches in a precomputed database, robustness and real-time capability are ensured
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: In the online phase, model discovery reduces to a sequence of algebraic operations and similarity searches within a precomputed database, which ensures robustness and real-time capability.

mechanism_principle.content: Convex and non-decreasing g, together with non-negative scaling and additive combination, make the isotropic strain energy polyconvex.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The additional scaling by the non-negative homogeneity parameters θ preserves convexity, and since sums of convex functions remain convex, the isotropic contribution to the strain energy is polyconvex provided that g is convex and non-decreasing.

mechanism_principle.content: Because composition of a convex, non-decreasing function with a convex argument remains convex, the anisotropic contribution is polyconvex if h has those properties.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Since the composition of a convex, non-decreasing function with a convex argument remains convex, the anisotropic contribution to the strain energy is polyconvex as well, provided that h satisfies these properties.

mechanism_principle.content: When the derivative bound is exceeded, replacing the exponential by a second-order Taylor expansion controls growth and preserves local C2 consistency at the switching point.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
If the bound is exceeded, the exponential term is replaced by its second-order Taylor expansion around the corresponding point x0, implicitly defined by |f ′(x0)| = τ,

This ensures controlled growth and local C2 consistency at the switching point.
